You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- What the test sets up:
  - Two mutually exclusive groups:
    - group1: options a and b
    - group2: options x and y
  - Command line args: ["-a"]
  - Default properties: b=true, x=true
  - Expected behavior: since a and b are in the same OptionGroup, providing -a on the command line should prevent b from being accepted from defaults; x should be accepted from defaults because no option from group2 is on the command line.

- How parsing currently works:
  - Parser.parse(Options, String[], Properties, boolean) clears prior state, then processes command-line tokens, then processes properties, then checks required options (lines 241–244).
  - For command-line tokens, processOption:
    - Clones the Option, calls updateRequiredOptions(opt) before adding it to the CommandLine (lines 383–394).
    - updateRequiredOptions sets the selected option in the corresponding OptionGroup and, in typical implementations, throws if another option from the same group was already selected (lines 410–422).
  - For defaults, processProperties(Properties):
    - Skips if cmd already has the option (lines 263–265).
    - Retrieves the Option and processes any argument value (lines 265–293).
    - Critically, it adds the option to the CommandLine first, then calls updateRequiredOptions(opt) afterwards (lines 295–296).
    - There is even a comment noting the missing group logic: “if the option is part of a group, check if another option of the group has been selected” (lines 267–269), but no such check is implemented.

- Why the bug occurs with the test data:
  - The command line selects -a. During token processing, updateRequiredOptions marks a as the selected member of group1.
  - When properties are processed:
    - b is not yet present in cmd, so it is considered.
    - processProperties adds b to the CommandLine first (cmd.addOption(opt)) and only then calls updateRequiredOptions(opt).
    - Because there is no pre-check against the OptionGroup selection, and the update is done after adding, the code neither prevents nor rejects b before it’s added. The comment indicates this check was intended but missing.
    - As a result, both a and b end up on the CommandLine, violating the mutual exclusion.
  - For group2, x=true is added from properties as expected since no conflicting option was provided on the command line.

- Cross-check with the issue report:
  - The report states that the state of option groups is neither checked nor updated when processing default options, allowing mutually exclusive options to coexist if one comes from the CLI and one from defaults. This precisely matches the behavior in processProperties: missing group check and reversed order of updateRequiredOptions versus addOption.

- Contributing code details:
  - parse processes properties only after command-line tokens (line 241), so conflicts must be detected in processProperties.
  - processProperties contains a placeholder comment about checking group selection (lines 267–269) but performs no such logic.
  - It also calls updateRequiredOptions after adding to cmd (lines 295–296), unlike processOption which does the update before adding, further undermining conflict detection.

In summary, defaults (Properties) are applied without respecting OptionGroup exclusivity because processProperties does not check group selection before adding the option and updates group state only afterward. This allows b to be added in spite of a already being selected, causing the test to fail.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
